native_result.query: How does the prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening vary based on habitat type?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: Non-native plants introduced via gardening make up a markedly larger share of the invaded non-native flora in wet, coastal and forested habitats than in croplands and urban habitats: gardening accounts for ~56% of non-native records in wetlands, ~53% in coastal habitats and ~88-100% in forest plots (sparse, <=8 records), versus ~19% in croplands and ~30% in urban plots, where unintentional introductions dominate (chi2=75.2, df=18, permutation p=0.0002). In absolute per-plot terms the views diverge: gardening species are most frequent in urban, coastal, wetland and riparian plots (0.6-0.8 records/plot; present in 36-50% of plots) because these habitats are most heavily invaded overall (1.4-2.3 records/plot), while croplands are dominated by unintentional introductions. Estimates for rock outcrops, scrublands and both forest types rest on <=8 records and are unstable.
native_result.WorkflowB: Firth-penalized logistic GLMs (habitat factor, ref=Croplands) on (1) gardening share of 481 invaded-species records per habitat, (2) gardening presence across all 632 plots; Monte-Carlo permutation chi-square (10,000 perms, habitat margins fixed) for pathway x habitat association; per-habitat Wilson CIs and Fisher exact tests with BH correction; overdispersion diagnostic; sparse habitats (<=8 records) flagged, not collapsed; phylogeny used only to confirm tip-taxon match (81/81); temporal trends mentioned as one-line context.

sub_hypo.context: Non-native flora in Barcelona province; 481 invaded-species records grouped by habitat. Forest estimates are based on sparse samples of at most 8 records.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening share (n.gard/n.total) is approximately 56% in wetlands, 53% in coastal habitats and 88–100% in forest plots, compared with 19% in croplands and 30% in urban plots. Unintentional introductions dominate croplands and urban habitats. Pathway and habitat are associated (chi-square=75.2, df=18, permutation p=0.0002; 10,000 permutations with habitat margins fixed). Gardening share is modeled with a Firth-penalized logistic GLM using croplands as the reference habitat.

sub_hypo.text: Despite their lower proportional representation in urban habitats, gardening species are most frequent in absolute per-plot terms in urban, coastal, wetland and riparian plots, which are the most heavily invaded habitats overall; croplands are dominated by unintentional introductions.
sub_hypo.context: All 632 sampled plots in Barcelona province, including plots without gardening introductions.
sub_hypo.relations: Urban, coastal, wetland and riparian habitats have 0.6–0.8 gardening records per plot, gardening presence in 36–50% of plots, and overall invasion frequencies of 1.4–2.3 records per plot. Thus, absolute gardening frequency and proportional gardening share give different habitat comparisons. Gardening presence (n.gard>0) is modeled with a Firth-penalized logistic GLM using croplands as the reference habitat.
